questions.question:
**Read the below statement:**

1. Solicitor General of India is appointed by the president of India.

2. A candidate contesting for the post of the President of India is required to make a security deposit of ₹15,000.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statement 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **security deposit of ₹15,000** is mandatory for candidates contesting the election for the President of India, as per **Article 58 of the Constitution of India** and the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952.
 
• The deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to secure at least one-sixth of the votes cast in the election.
 
• The security deposit ensures that only serious candidates participate in the election process.
 
• The election of the President of India is conducted by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories.
 
• As per the rules, the nomination paper must be supported by at least **50 proposers and 50 seconders** to ensure legitimacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statement 1: Solicitor General of India is appointed by the president of India**

 
 
• The Solicitor General of India is the **second-highest law officer** in the country after the Attorney General of India.
 
• Unlike the Attorney General, the Solicitor General is not appointed directly by the President of India. Instead, the appointment is made by the **Union Government**, specifically by the Ministry of Law and Justice.
 
• The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General in performing legal duties and advises the government on legal matters.
 
• Therefore, **Statement 1 is incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Presidential Elections in India:**
 
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college through a proportional representation system using a single transferable vote.
 
• Every member of the electoral college casts their vote, and the candidate receiving the highest number of votes is elected.
 
• The process is governed by the provisions in **Articles 52 to 62** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Facts:**
 
 
• The President of India serves a term of five years and can be re-elected.
 
• The eligibility criteria for candidates contesting the Presidential elections include being a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• In case of vacancy, the election must be held within six months.

questions.question:
Based on the given statements which option is **correct**:

**Statement I:** Mathura art produced images for both Indian and non-Indian patrons.

**Statement II:** Mathura art ignored nature-based themes in its sculptures.

options.text: Statement I and II both are Correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Only Statement I is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement I is correct:** Mathura art was a significant school of art during the Kushana period, producing sculptures for both Indian and non-Indian patrons, including images of Buddha, Bodhisattvas, Yakshas, and Jain Tirthankaras.
 
• Mathura art is renowned for its syncretic style, blending indigenous Indian artistic traditions with Greco-Roman influences.
 
• It catered to diverse religious communities like Buddhists, Jains, and Hindus, reflecting its inclusive nature and wide patronage.
 
• Mathura art produced sculptures for Buddhist stupas in India and beyond, including regions such as Central Asia, showcasing its appeal to non-Indian patrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statement II is incorrect:** Mathura art did not ignore nature-based themes. In fact:

 
 
• It prominently featured nature-inspired motifs such as trees, animals, and floral designs in its sculptures.
 
• Yakshas and Yakshinis, celestial beings associated with nature and fertility, were frequently depicted in Mathura sculptures.
 
• Nature was often used symbolically in Buddhist and Jain art, such as the Bodhi tree representing Buddha's enlightenment.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Mathura Art:**
 
 
• Mathura art evolved during the Kushana period and served as a major center of artistic activity.
 
• It is characterized by red sandstone sculptures with intricate detailing and bold expressions.
 
• The art form emphasized realism and depicted human and divine figures with naturalistic features and elaborate ornamentation.
 
• Notable examples include the seated Buddha statues and images of Hindu deities like Vishnu and Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Gandhara Art:**
 
 
• While Mathura art represented indigenous Indian styles, Gandhara art reflected strong Greco-Roman influences.
 
• Mathura sculptures were made of red sandstone, whereas Gandhara sculptures predominantly used grey schist stone.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Hola Mohalla festival of Punjab is **correct**?

options.text: It is celebrated mainly by women through crafts and songs in Patiala.
It showcases martial arts, langars, and Nihang mock battles at Anandpur Sahib.
It is a harvest festival observed in Punjab just before Diwali.
Hola Mohalla is celebrated on the same day as Holi.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It showcases martial arts, langars, and Nihang mock battles at Anandpur Sahib.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hola Mohalla** is a Sikh festival that was first introduced by Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, in 1701.
 
• The festival is celebrated a day after Holi and is marked by demonstrations of **martial arts, mock battles by Nihang warriors, and traditional Sikh customs**.
 
• The main celebrations are held at **Anandpur Sahib**, a significant Sikh pilgrimage site in Punjab.
 
• It is known for its **community kitchens (langars)**, where free meals are served to all visitors as part of Sikh tradition.
 
• The festival also includes **religious processions, poetry recitations, and devotional music**, making it a vibrant cultural and spiritual event.

• It seems to be a misrepresentation of certain other cultural festivals in Punjab where women actively participate in folk activities like *Giddha* and *Phulkari*.
 
• In Punjab, **Baisakhi** is the prominent harvest festival celebrated in April to mark the wheat harvesting season.
 
• Hola Mohalla is celebrated **a day after Holi** and is distinct in its focus on martial traditions and Sikh spiritual values.

questions.question: In freestyle wrestling, which of the following actions can result in a technical point for the wrestler?

options.text: Running out of the mat deliberately

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Performing a successful takedown**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A takedown is a critical technique in freestyle wrestling that allows a wrestler to bring their opponent from a standing position to the mat and gain control.
 
• Performing a successful takedown awards the wrestler technical points, which depend on the skill level and execution of the move (usually 2 to 5 points).
 
• Common types of takedowns include single-leg takedown, double-leg takedown, and throws.
 
• In addition to scoring points, a takedown puts the wrestler in an advantageous position to attempt further scoring or pinning.
 
• Freestyle wrestling emphasizes both offensive and defensive techniques, with takedowns being one of the primary methods of scoring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Running out of the mat deliberately**

 
 
• Running out of the mat is considered a form of passive wrestling or avoiding engagement, which can lead to penalties.
 
• Instead of gaining points, wrestlers may receive warnings or penalties for deliberately stepping out of the mat to escape an opponent’s hold or avoid engagement.
 
• In some cases, referees may award points to the opponent if this action is deemed intentional.
 
 
 
• **Holding the opponent's singlet**
 
 
• Grabbing the opponent's singlet, headgear, or other parts of their uniform is prohibited in freestyle wrestling.
 
• This action is considered illegal and results in penalties or warnings against the wrestler committing the foul.
 
• The purpose of this rule is to ensure fairness and maintain the integrity of the sport.
 
 
 
• **Using an illegal headlock**
 
 
• An illegal headlock occurs when a wrestler applies a headlock without an arm included in the hold.
 
• This technique is not allowed as it can cause serious injuries and is against the rules of freestyle wrestling.
 
• Wrestlers using illegal holds may face penalties, warnings, or even disqualification in extreme cases.

questions.question: Vijender Singh defeated which player in the quarter-finals to secure India's first Olympic boxing medal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carlos Góngora**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vijender Singh defeated **Carlos Góngora**, a boxer from Ecuador, in the quarter-finals of the Men's Middleweight category at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
 
• This victory secured Vijender Singh a medal in boxing, making him the first Indian boxer to win an Olympic medal.
 
• The match was intensely fought, with Vijender showcasing exceptional strategy, precision, and stamina to outclass Carlos Góngora.
 
• Vijender's performance at the Beijing Olympics marked a milestone for Indian boxing, elevating the sport's status in the country.
 
• He eventually secured the bronze medal in the Men's Middleweight (75 kg) category, creating history for Indian sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emilio Correa:**

 
 
• Emilio Correa is a Cuban boxer who competed in the Middleweight category at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
 
• He won the silver medal in the event, losing to James DeGale of Great Britain in the final.
 
• Correa was known for his aggressive fighting style and strong punches in the competition.
 
 
 
• **Misha Aloyan:**
 
 
• Misha Aloyan is a Russian boxer who specializes in the Flyweight category.
 
• He is a two-time world champion and an Olympic medalist, winning the bronze medal at the 2012 London Olympics.
 
• However, Aloyan did not compete in the same weight category or event as Vijender Singh during the 2008 Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Vasyl Lomachenko:**
 
 
• Vasyl Lomachenko is a celebrated Ukrainian boxer, widely regarded as one of the greatest amateur boxers of all time.
 
• He won gold medals in the Featherweight and Lightweight categories at the 2008 and 2012 Olympics respectively.
 
• Despite his legendary status, Lomachenko competed in a different weight category than Vijender Singh during the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

questions.question: Which mechanism did India operationalize in 2024 to strengthen regional financial resilience within SAARC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SAARC Currency Swap Framework (2024-27)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SAARC Currency Swap Framework (2024-27) was operationalized by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to enhance financial cooperation and stability among SAARC member nations.
 
• Under this mechanism, India provides short-term financial assistance in foreign currency to SAARC member countries facing liquidity constraints.
 
• The total corpus for the framework is USD 2 billion, with each eligible member country allowed to withdraw up to USD 400 million within specified limits.
 
• The framework aims to strengthen regional financial resilience, mitigate balance of payment crises, and promote economic stability within the SAARC region.
 
• The currency swap facility is offered in major international currencies (e.g., USD, EUR) or Indian Rupees to support member nations in times of financial distress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SAARC Development Fund (SDF) capital increase**:

 
 
• The SAARC Development Fund was established in 2010 to promote regional integration and economic development in SAARC member states.
 
• It primarily funds projects under its three windows: Social, Economic, and Infrastructure development.
 
• Although increasing the SDF's capital has been proposed, it is not directly linked to the financial resilience mechanisms implemented in 2024.
 
 
 
• **About SAARC**:
 
 
• The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established in 1985 to promote economic, social, and cultural cooperation among its eight member states: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.
 
• SAARC initiatives aim to foster regional integration, address common challenges, and promote sustainable development within South Asia.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks: Established in 1961 within the former Palace of the Maharaja of Patiala, the National Institute of Sports was later renamed as the Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS) on ______ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23rd January 1973**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Institute of Sports (NIS) was established in 1961 within the premises of the historic Palace of the Maharaja of Patiala, Punjab.
 
• It was renamed as the **Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports (NSNIS)** on **23rd January 1973**.
 
• The renaming was done in honor of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, a prominent leader in India’s freedom struggle, whose birth anniversary falls on January 23rd.
 
• NSNIS is widely regarded as the "Mecca" of Indian sports, providing professional training and technical education in various sports disciplines.
 
• It functions under the aegis of the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)** and plays a pivotal role in nurturing and developing athletes and sports coaches in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Institute of Sports (NIS) and its importance**:

 
 
• The institute offers advanced training programs for athletes and coaches in a range of disciplines, including athletics, hockey, football, boxing, and wrestling.
 
• It also conducts diploma and certification courses in sports coaching, equipping individuals with the skills to train athletes effectively.
 
• NSNIS has played a key role in producing several Olympians and international-level athletes for India.
 
• It continues to be a hub for sports research and the development of modern training methodologies.

questions.question:
Which statements **accurately **describe water bodies in the Indian Desert?

1. Streams are perennial and flow year-round.

2. Most streams disappear into the sand.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Only 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Desert, also known as the Thar Desert, is one of the most arid regions in India, and water scarcity is a defining feature of this landscape.
 
• Most streams in the Indian Desert are ephemeral in nature, meaning they flow only during the monsoon season and disappear into the sand due to high porosity and evaporation rates.
 
• Perennial streams are rare in the Thar Desert as the region receives an average annual rainfall of only 100-500 mm, which is insufficient to sustain year-round water flow.
 
• One notable exception is the Luni River, which is the largest river in the Thar Desert but even it becomes saline after flowing through the desert region, limiting its usability.
 
• The hydrological characteristic of the Thar Desert is such that most of the water from surface streams infiltrates into the sandy terrain or evaporates quickly due to the high temperatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Indian Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert covers approximately 200,000 square kilometers, making it the world's 17th largest desert.
 
• The region is characterized by sand dunes, rocky outcrops, and sparse vegetation.
 
• Oases in the Thar Desert, such as those in Jaisalmer, provide limited water resources for the local population.
 
• The region supports unique flora and fauna adapted to the arid environment, such as desert foxes and thorny shrubs.

questions.question:
Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): Demographic statistics like birth and death rates rely on accurate reporting by households.

Reason (R): Birth and death registration is mandatory and always accurately followed in all parts of India.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Demographic statistics** like birth and death rates depend heavily on accurate reporting from households to maintain the reliability of population data.
 
• Birth and death registration in India is governed by the **Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969**, which mandates recording these events.
 
• Despite the legal requirement, the implementation of birth and death registration varies widely across regions due to factors like literacy levels, infrastructure, and accessibility.
 
• The claim in the reason (R) that registration is "always accurately followed in all parts of India" is incorrect. Challenges such as lack of awareness, geographical inaccessibility, and resource constraints often result in underreporting or delayed registration.
 
• Thus, while the assertion (A) is correct, the reason (R) is false, as it does not accurately explain the situation of registration compliance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance of Birth and Death Registration**

 
 
• Accurate registration is crucial for demographic analysis, policy-making, and resource allocation at both national and state levels.
 
• Birth certificates serve as proof of age, identity, and nationality, which are essential for accessing various benefits and rights.
 
• Death registration helps track mortality rates, causes of death, and contributes to public health planning.
 
• Efforts are being made to improve registration rates in India through awareness campaigns and the digitization of records.

questions.question: The term "pleiotropy" refers to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One gene affects multiple traits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pleiotropy** refers to a situation where a single gene affects multiple phenotypic traits.
 
• This occurs because the gene encodes a product (such as a protein) that is involved in multiple biological processes.
 
• Examples of pleiotropy include the gene responsible for sickle-cell anemia, which affects red blood cell shape and provides resistance to malaria.
 
• Pleiotropic effects can be observed in both normal physiological processes and genetic disorders.
 
• Pleiotropy is a fundamental concept in genetics and demonstrates how genes can have far-reaching effects on an organism's phenotype.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Multiple genes affect one trait**

 
 
• This describes a phenomenon known as **polygenic inheritance**, where a trait is governed by two or more genes.
 
• Examples include human height, skin color, and eye color, which result from the combined effect of several genes.
 
• Polygenic traits often show continuous variation, unlike pleiotropic traits, which are influenced by a single gene.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Gene mutation in one allele**
 
 
• This refers to a mutation in one copy of a gene (allele) that can affect its function.
 
• Such mutations can lead to genetic disorders if the mutated allele is dominant or if the condition is recessive and both alleles are affected.
 
• While this is a distinct genetic concept, it does not describe pleiotropy.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Gene duplication**
 
 
• Gene duplication is an evolutionary process where a segment of DNA containing a gene is copied, resulting in multiple copies of that gene in the genome.
 
• This can lead to the evolution of new gene functions or increased gene dosage but is unrelated to pleiotropy.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Pleiotropy:**
 
 
• Pleiotropy is critical for understanding the complexity of genetic interactions and how single genes can have multiple impacts on an organism's physiology and development.
 
• It is also significant in studying diseases with pleiotropic effects, such as Marfan syndrome, where a single gene mutation affects the connective tissue throughout the body.

questions.question: How are Money Bills handled in both Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures with bicameralism under the Constitution?

options.text: Rajya Sabha must approve Money Bills within 14 days
In States, the Legislative Council can amend a Money Bill within 14 days
Both Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils have equal powers on Money Bills
Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils can only make recommendations within 14 days

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils can only make recommendations within 14 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and not in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Once the Lok Sabha passes a Money Bill, it is sent to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations, but the Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject it.
 
• The Rajya Sabha must return the Money Bill to the Lok Sabha with or without recommendations within a period of 14 days. If not returned within this period, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses of Parliament.
 
• In the case of State Legislatures with bicameralism, the Legislative Council can only make recommendations to the Legislative Assembly on Money Bills and must return the Bill within 14 days.
 
• The powers of the Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Councils on Money Bills are limited to recommendations, and the final decision rests with the Lok Sabha and the Legislative Assembly, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A Money Bill deals exclusively with matters listed in Article 110(1) of the Constitution, such as taxation, borrowing, expenditure, and matters incidental to these.
 
• The distinction between Money Bills and other financial Bills is significant because it limits the role of the Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils in the legislative process.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Legislative Assembly is the final authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill.

questions.question: It is difficult to start motion with a heavy box and also difficult to stop it once it's moving. This best exemplifies:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Property of inertia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Inertia** is the property of matter that causes it to resist changes in its state of motion or rest unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• It is a fundamental concept of classical mechanics, based on **Newton's First Law of Motion**, which states that "an object at rest remains at rest, and an object in motion continues in motion with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an external force."
 
• The difficulty in starting the motion of a heavy box is due to its **inertia of rest**, which resists any change from a stationary state.
 
• Similarly, the difficulty in stopping the box once it is moving is due to its **inertia of motion**, which resists any change in its current velocity.
 
• The larger the mass of an object, the greater its inertia, which is why heavier objects are harder to start or stop in motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concept of Power:**
 
 
• Power is defined as the **rate at which work is done or energy is transferred** over time.
 
• The formula for power is given as **P = W/t**, where P is power, W is work, and t is the time taken.
 
• It is measured in Watts (W) in the SI system.
 
• Power is not directly related to the resistance to motion or stopping, and hence it is not the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• This principle states that **energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only change from one form to another**.
 
• The total energy in an isolated system remains constant over time.
 
• While conservation of energy is a fundamental concept in physics, it does not directly explain the difficulty in starting or stopping the motion of a heavy object.
 
 
 
• **Action-Reaction Principle:**
 
 
• Based on **Newton's Third Law of Motion**, this principle states that "for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction."
 
• It explains how forces act in pairs, such as when you push against a wall and the wall pushes back with an equal and opposite force.
 
• Although this principle is crucial in understanding motion, it does not account for the resistance to changes in motion, which is the domain of inertia.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita (BNS), 2023, consolidates and amends provisions related to which branch of law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Criminal Substantive Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita (BNS), 2023, is aimed at consolidating and amending laws related to **Criminal Substantive Law** in India.
 
• BNS is designed as a replacement for the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860, which was drafted during British colonial rule in India.
 
• The primary objective of the BNS is to modernize and reform criminal laws to align with the changing socio-economic and technological landscape of the country.
 
• It seeks to simplify criminal laws, ensure speedy justice, and address contemporary challenges such as cybercrime and organized crime.
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita Bill, 2023, was introduced in Parliament in August 2023 as part of a broader initiative to overhaul colonial-era legal frameworks, including the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) and the Indian Evidence Act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Civil Procedure Law**

 
 
• Civil Procedure Law governs the procedures and practices in civil courts, such as filing lawsuits, conducting trials, and enforcing judgments.
 
• The primary legislation governing this branch in India is the **Civil Procedure Code (CPC), 1908**.
 
• Civil laws deal with private disputes between individuals or organizations, such as property disputes, contracts, or family matters.
 
 
 
• **Evidence Law**
 
 
• The law of evidence deals with the rules and principles that determine what evidence is admissible in courts.
 
• The **Indian Evidence Act, 1872**, is the governing framework for evidence-related matters in Indian courts.
 
• It specifies the type and manner of evidence that can be presented in civil or criminal cases, including oral, documentary, and circumstantial evidence.
 
 
 
• **Contract Law**
 
 
• Contract law governs agreements between parties that are enforceable by law.
 
• The primary legislation in India is the **Indian Contract Act, 1872**, which outlines the essentials of a valid contract, including offer, acceptance, consideration, and capacity to contract.
 
• It also covers specific contracts such as indemnity, guarantee, bailment, agency, and partnership agreements.

questions.question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

Assertion (A): The National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to reduce dependency on fossil fuels.

Reason (R): It is implemented by MoEFCC.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Green Hydrogen Mission** was approved by the Indian government in January 2023 with the aim of making India a global hub for green hydrogen production and export.
 
• The mission primarily focuses on **reducing dependency on fossil fuels** by promoting green hydrogen, a clean and sustainable energy source derived from renewable energy sources like solar and wind power.
 
• Through this mission, India aims to produce 5 million metric tonnes of green hydrogen annually by 2030, reducing carbon emissions and aiding the country's energy transition.
 
• The mission is led by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**, not the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).
 
• The mission also seeks to attract investments, create employment opportunities, and position India as a leader in the global green hydrogen economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Focus of the National Green Hydrogen Mission:**

 
 
• Promotes the use of green hydrogen in industries such as steel, chemicals, and transportation to reduce carbon footprints.
 
• Encourages research and development (R&D) to advance green hydrogen technologies and infrastructure.
 
• Aims to reduce import dependency on fossil fuels, supporting India's energy security.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC):**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for implementing policies and programs related to the conservation of the environment, forests, and climate change mitigation.
 
• It oversees various environmental clearance processes, biodiversity conservation efforts, and initiatives to combat climate change.
 
• Although it plays a significant role in environmental sustainability, it is not directly involved in implementing the National Green Hydrogen Mission.

questions.question:
**Fill in the Blank:**

Koli dance is traditionally performed by the ______ community.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fisherfolk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Koli dance** is a traditional folk dance performed by the **Koli community**, primarily comprising fisherfolk in Maharashtra, India.
 
• The dance represents the culture, lifestyle, and livelihood of the fishing community, symbolizing their connection with the sea and fishing activities.
 
• Koli dance is characterized by synchronized movements, vibrant costumes, and rhythmic music that depict the daily lives of fisherfolk, including fishing techniques and boat rowing.
 
• The dance is performed during community celebrations, festivals, and special occasions to express joy and unity.
 
• The Koli community has a rich cultural heritage, and their dance is an important representation of their identity and traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Popular Folk Dances of Maharashtra:**

 
 
• Lavani: A dynamic dance with powerful rhythms, often performed by women in nine-yard sarees, narrating stories of love, society, and politics. 
 
• Tamasha: A traditional folk theatre with dance, music, and drama, known for its entertainment and social commentary. 
 
• Koli Dance: A lively dance of the Koli fishing community, reflecting their daily life and traditions. 
 
• Lezim: An energetic dance performed with small cymbals (lezim), popular in processions and celebrations. 
 
• Powada: A ballad form narrating the heroic tales of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. 
 
• Dindi & Kala: Devotional dances performed during religious festivals, often honoring Lord Vithoba. 
 
• Gondhal: A ritualistic dance performed for deities like Goddess Renuka. 
 
• Dhangari Gaja: A dance performed solely by men, originating from the Dhangar (shepherd) community.

questions.question: The Global Energy Transition Index 2025 is released by which international organization?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Economic Forum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Global Energy Transition Index** is released by the World Economic Forum (WEF), a Swiss-based international organization committed to improving the state of the world.
 
• This index assesses the energy systems of countries based on factors like environmental sustainability, energy security, and affordability, focusing on their readiness for energy transition.
 
• The index uses a unique framework called the **Energy Transition Readiness Framework**, considering both current performance and enabling conditions for energy transition.
 
• It ranks countries based on their ability to adopt clean energy technologies, reduce carbon emissions, and ensure reliable access to energy.
 
• The WEF works closely with governments, businesses, and other stakeholders to provide actionable insights for achieving sustainable energy transitions globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **IRENA (International Renewable Energy Agency)**

 
 
• IRENA is an intergovernmental organization that supports countries in their transition to sustainable energy.
 
• It primarily focuses on promoting renewable energy sources like solar, wind, and hydroelectric power.
 
• Its reports and initiatives emphasize renewable energy deployment, innovation, and policy frameworks worldwide.
 
• While IRENA plays a key role in global energy discussions, it does not release the Global Energy Transition Index.
 
 
 
• **IEA (International Energy Agency)**
 
 
• IEA is an autonomous agency established in the framework of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
 
• It focuses on energy security, economic development, and environmental sustainability across member countries.
 
• IEA releases reports like the World Energy Outlook and Energy Technology Perspectives.
 
 
 
• **UNDP (United Nations Development Programme)**
 
 
• UNDP is a global development network under the United Nations, focusing on sustainable development, poverty alleviation, and climate change.
 
• Its energy-related work often involves improving energy access and promoting clean energy solutions in developing countries.

questions.question: Which of the following is **correctly **classified as a consumer goods industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Toothpaste**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Consumer goods industries** produce goods that are directly consumed by customers, meaning they do not require further processing.
 
• **Toothpaste** is a prime example of a consumer goods product as it is manufactured for direct use by individuals for personal hygiene.
 
• It falls under the category of **FMCG (Fast-Moving Consumer Goods)**, which are frequently purchased, low-cost items such as toiletries, beverages, and packaged food products.
 
• Consumer goods industries focus on manufacturing products that cater to everyday needs, including items like toothpaste, soap, cosmetics, and food products.
 
• Products from consumer goods industries are typically mass-produced to meet the demand of a large consumer base and distributed through retail outlets or e-commerce platforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron and steel:**

 
 
• The iron and steel industry is classified as a **heavy industry** as it deals with large-scale production of materials used in infrastructure, construction, and manufacturing.
 
• It provides raw materials for industries like automobile manufacturing, shipbuilding, and machinery production.
 
• Steel is not a consumer product but an **intermediate good**, which requires further processing to create consumer or industrial goods.
 
 
 
• **Aluminium smelting:**
 
 
• Aluminium smelting is an industrial process that involves the extraction of aluminium from its ore, bauxite, using electrolytic reduction.
 
• This industry is classified as a **basic or heavy industry** because aluminium is an intermediate product used in manufacturing sectors such as transportation, construction, and packaging.
 
• It does not directly produce goods for consumer use but supports other industries by providing raw materials.
 
 
 
• **Copper smelting:**
 
 
• Copper smelting involves the extraction of copper metal from its ores through heating and chemical processes.
 
• It is a **heavy or basic industry**, as the copper produced is used in electrical wiring, plumbing, and industrial machinery.
 
• Like aluminium and steel, copper is an intermediate product and not directly consumed by individuals.

questions.question: Article 246A of the Constitution of India gives power to both Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taxation of Goods and Services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 246A of the Indian Constitution was introduced through the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**, which enabled the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
 
• It grants **concurrent powers** to both the Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws with respect to GST.
 
• Under this article, the Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on **inter-state trade or commerce of goods and services**, while both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate on intra-state transactions.
 
• GST subsumes multiple indirect taxes such as VAT, Service Tax, Excise Duty, and others, simplifying India's indirect taxation system.
 
• The introduction of Article 246A aimed to promote a unified market, enhance ease of doing business, and eliminate the cascading effects of taxes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Property Rights (Option 1):**

 
 
• Property rights in India are addressed under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution, which states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
 
• Initially, property rights were a fundamental right under Article 31, but it was abolished by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and made a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• This provision ensures that private property cannot be taken away without due process of law or proper compensation.
 
 
 
• **Emergency Provisions (Option 3):**
 
 
• Emergency provisions are detailed under Part XVIII (Articles 352 to 360) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These provisions enable the government to assume greater control during times of crisis and include three types of emergencies: National Emergency (Article 352), State Emergency/President’s Rule (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360).
 
• These provisions are invoked to safeguard the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India during extraordinary situations.
 
 
 
• **Criminal Law (Option 4):**
 
 
• Criminal law in India is primarily governed by the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973, and various special laws.
 
• The Parliament and state legislatures can legislate on criminal law under the Concurrent List (List III) of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.
 
• Criminal law ensures the maintenance of public order, punishment for offenses, and the protection of citizens’ rights.

questions.question:
**Consider the following statements:**

1. Supreme Court can transfer cases from one High Court to another.

2. Article 139A was introduced by the 42nd Amendment.

Which of the above is/are **correct?**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1: Supreme Court can transfer cases from one High Court to another** – Article 139A of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to transfer cases involving the same or substantially the same question of law from one High Court to another to ensure uniformity in decisions.
 
• This provision is aimed at eliminating conflicting judgments by different High Courts on the same legal matter, thereby ensuring consistency in the interpretation of laws across the country.
 
• **Statement 2: Article 139A was introduced by the 42nd Amendment** – The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added Article 139A to the Indian Constitution. This amendment is often referred to as the "mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it introduced.
 
• Article 139A allows the Supreme Court to withdraw cases from one or more High Courts if it feels that these cases involve a substantial question of law of general importance.
 
• Both statements are correct, as Article 139A was indeed introduced by the 42nd Amendment, and it authorizes the Supreme Court to transfer cases between High Courts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment of 1976:**

 
 
• Known as the "mini-Constitution," this amendment brought significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added several articles, including Article 139A, and amended many existing provisions to strengthen the central government's powers.
 
• Key changes included the addition of the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) and the insertion of the words "Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity" into the Preamble.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court’s Powers under Article 139A:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has the authority to transfer cases between High Courts or withdraw cases from High Courts to itself if substantial questions of law are involved.
 
• This provision ensures uniformity in the interpretation of laws across different jurisdictions in India.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Transfers under Article 139A:**
 
 
• This article is critical for maintaining judicial discipline and consistency in legal interpretations by higher judiciary bodies.
 
• Such transfers are often considered in cases involving constitutional interpretation or significant questions of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Role of High Courts:**
 
 
• High Courts are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in India, but their decisions may differ based on regional contexts.
 
• Article 139A ensures that conflicting decisions on similar issues are avoided by centralizing the matter in the Supreme Court.
